newsitem.title: USA: Marion Cty, W. Va., delays school bond referendum.
newsitem.headline: Marion Cty, W. Va., delays school bond referendum.

text.p: West Virginia's Marion County School board voted Thursday to indefinitely delay a $33.3 million bond referendum that had been scheduled for Feb. 15.
Acting school superintendent Dennis Edge said the board had several concerns but that mainly, "There was a great concern about the size of the bond."
Edge said the general obligation bond issue would have raised property taxes by "a significant amount" in the county of less than 60,000 residents.
He said the bond issue was on indefinite hold while board members reassess school construction needs and the local economy.

Marion County residents approved their last two bond referendums, including a $12.3 million, seven-year issue for a new high school that will be paid off in March, and a $3.2 million issue last year for vocational school repairs.
But before that, "We had a long period of time, 30 years or so, there were no bond issues passed," Edge said.
